Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Setup 3 Your Turn 4 End of Game 5 Scoring 5.1 Total Rankings 6 Level of Difficulty 7 Hint card distribution Objective To work together as a team and gather the Yokai (four each of four suits: Foxes, River Children, Long-neck Women and Demons) by families. Setup The Yokai cards are shuffled and placed in a 4x4 grid. A stack of hint cards (7 for two players, 9 for three, 10 for four) is placed nearby. Your Turn You must do 3 actions in this order: Look at 2 cards, one by one. They don't have to be adjacent. Choose an uncovered Yokai card and move it. After the move, the 16 cards must still form a connected whole. Draw and reveal a hint card, or place a revealed hint card on a Yokai. A Yokai with a hint card is locked and cannot be looked at or moved. End of Game The game is ended when: Instead of doing any actions, a player declares the Yokai are gathered by families, or; All the hint cards are used. Once the game is over, flip over all Yokai. If the Yokai are grouped by families, the players win. Otherwise they lose. Scoring Victories are scored by hint card usage: 1 point per correctly placed hint card -1 point per incorrectly placed hint card 2 points per revealed but unused hint card 5 points per unrevealed hint card Total Rankings 0-10 points is an Honourable victory 11-14 points is a Glorious victory 15+ points is a Legendary victory Level of Difficulty If you win a game at a given level of difficulty, you can try the same level for a higher score or move on to the next level. Level 1: Basic rules. Level 2: Add a random affinity card which is only visible to the first player. The shown families must be adjacent at the end of the game. Level 3: Stack hint cards when revealing them. You may only place the last revealed hint. Level 4: Don't reveal hints. Instead take the top card and put it down beside the deck facedown. Level 5: Add a random objective card, visible to all. The cards must be in the indicated shape at the end of the game. Hint card distribution In a two-player game, there are 2 random single-colour cards, 3 two-colour cards and 2 three-colour cards. In a three-player game, there are 2 random single-colour cards, 4 two-colour cards and 3 three-colour cards. In a four-player game, there are 3 random single-colour cards, 4 two-colour cards and 3 three-colour cards. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] It's a cooperative memory game with no talking. I'm sure there's a type of person out there who enjoys games like this, but it's definitely not me.

[Rating: 2/10] Cooperative game with rather too much focus on its memory-game type element, trying to remember all the information about the face-down cards as you and other players later manipulate them. That's not really where I want the focus of so much of my mental energy to be in a game so it's not really for me.

[Rating: 3/10] Cooperative memory game with very limited communication options.  This game is not for me.

[Rating: 3/10] Deduction cooperative game with too much of a memory element for me. Probably fun for the write group but really not a combination I enjoyed.

[Rating: 4/10] Co-op "Concentration", with the ability to move cards and give some hints thrown in. I don't generally enjoy memory games anyway, but the co-op aspect of this one didn't feel enjoyable to me either; players must spend some turns looking at the same cards other players just looked at, or no one will be on the same page. The basic game seems easy enough to win, as we won the first two times we played.

[Rating: 4/10] I'll keep playing until I win, but that's the only reason. Stubbornness.  Once the group grasps the spatial tricks, it gets easier. If that doesn't happen, get a new group or a new space.
